name: PubMedQA
intro: PubMedQA是一个基于PubMed摘要的生物医学问答数据集，任务是用“是”、“否”或“可能”回答研究问题。包含1000个专家标注、61200个未标注及211300个人工生成问答，是首个需对生物医学研究文本进行推理的数据集。
org: University of Pittsburgh, Carnegie Mellon University
build_method: PubMed摘要筛选, 医学专家标注, 规则与启发式生成
scale: 1K专家标注 + 61.2K未标注 + 211.3K启发式生成
build_method_en: PubMed abstract filtering, medical-expert annotation, rule-based and heuristic generation
intro_en: PubMedQA is a biomedical question answering dataset based on PubMed abstracts, where the task is to answer research questions with "yes," "no," or "maybe." It includes 1,000 expert-annotated, 61,200 unlabeled, and 211,300 artificially generated QA pairs, making it the first dataset requiring reasoning over biomedical research texts.
drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; status=source-reconstructed-awaiting-independent-signoff; scope=PubMedQA paper-aligned bilingual Build Process, official-release boundary, evaluator boundary, license boundary, and source-stage topology contract. Primary evidence is PubMedQA v1 at https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.06146v1 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.06146v1; the reviewed PDF SHA-256 is 190af87fa13a8edca51152dadf46e7cbddb5844544e1b32eb8d805a0ff390e3c. Official code is pinned to https://github.com/pubmedqa/pubmedqa/tree/1cbae8e92f72f20c8d3747cbb3bf5bc53554d997. The graph follows paper Section 3 rather than treating a baseline training schedule as benchmark construction. PubMed articles enter the natural-question branch only when the title contains a question mark and the structured abstract has a conclusive section. Each pre-PQA-U record uses the original title as question, the abstract without its conclusion as context, and the conclusion as long answer. PQA-L candidates are randomly sampled and first screened for yes/no/maybe answerability. Both annotators are qualified M.D. candidates, but their views are intentionally asymmetric: annotator 1 sees question, context, and long answer and produces the paper's reasoning-free annotation; annotator 2 sees question and context only and produces the reasoning-required annotation. If their labels agree, that label is used. If they disagree, they discuss; an item is removed if no agreement is reached. The resulting PQA-L contains exactly 1,000 items, with 55.2% yes, 33.8% no, and 11.0% maybe. A random 500 are used for 10-fold cross-validation and the remaining 500 are the held-out test set. PQA-U is a separate branch from pre-PQA-U: a rule removes questions beginning with wh-words and questions involving selection among multiple entities. The paper reports more than 93% agreement with annotator 1 for identifying yes/no/maybe-answerable questions and 61.2K retained unlabeled items; this is specifically rule-versus-annotator-1 answerability agreement, not the PQA-L inter-annotator label agreement. PQA-A is not derived from the natural-question branch. It selects statement titles with NP-(VBP/VBZ) POS structure and a structured abstract with a conclusion, converts titles to questions by moving or adding copulas or auxiliaries and revising for coherence, and assigns yes/no from verb negation. It contains 211.3K items, 92.8% yes and 7.2% no, with 200K randomly sampled for training and 11.3K for validation. The PQA-L reasoning-required evaluation supplies question plus context, keeps the conclusion hidden, requires one of yes/no/maybe for every test PMID, and reports Accuracy plus three-class macro-F1. At the fixed repository revision, README.md SHA-256 is 1338affd8530b416358b4ea40e6f1d6c935197352341bca2cf02288985a1fd99, data/ori_pqal.json SHA-256 is 8b3276be8942ebbd77f3ddcda12c1749bf0e490045a736fd8438ee40cf37a41d, data/test_ground_truth.json SHA-256 is 939fe566f09017d13b1ca64d2ddfee0bc2374b366048152997669cccedc44d51, and evaluation.py SHA-256 is 2838af5bb0ac18e301a9af57323c2d89784f153ddaf4f889329bfa04842099f8. The evaluator asserts that prediction keys equal all and only the held-out PMIDs and uses sklearn accuracy_score and macro-averaged f1_score. The repository LICENSE is MIT with SHA-256 8e75abc6136be91e5ae66dbb6dda07c8bc9dcc215ed3bc1ba3ae7fab7904777e. No judge model, generative scoring, hidden conclusion input, author identity beyond the paper's M.D.-candidate disclosure, or mandatory multi-phase training is inferred. English and Chinese specs have identical semantic IDs, node types, sizes, positions, styles, edge endpoints, edge types, edge styles, waypoints, and modules; every secondary edge explicitly sets dashed=true and no edge carries a label. Six source/spec/architecture paths and two SVG paths retain their canonical benchmark-local values. mermaid_flowchart remains null and both flowchart fallbacks remain empty.
